cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: You're making a vegan alternative to eggs, aren't you?

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Something that doesn't use animal products?

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Yes. I'm using chickpeas.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: I had two main aims when I first started looking for an alternative to eggs, but actually

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: I've found chickpeas have got more advantages.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: But how about your project on reusing waste food – you were looking at bread, weren't you?

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Yes. It's been hard work, but I've enjoyed it.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: The basic process was quite straightforward -breaking the stale bread down to a paste

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: then reforming it.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: But you were using 3-D printing, weren't you, to make the paste into biscuits?

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Yeah, I'd used that before, but in this project, I had time to play around with different

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: patterns for the biscuits and finding how I could add fruit and vegetables to make them a

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: more appetising colour, and I was really pleased with what I managed to produce.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: It must've been a great feeling to make something appetising out of bits of old bread

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: that would've been thrown away otherwise.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: It was.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: And I'm hoping that some of the restaurants in town will be interested in the biscuits.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: I'm going to send them some samples.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: I came across something on the internet yesterday that might interest you.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: It was a company that's developed touch-sensitive sensors for food labels.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: It's a special sort of label on the food package.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: When the label's smooth, the food is fresh and then when you can feel bumps on the label,

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: that means the food's gone bad.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: It started off as a project to help visually impaired people know whether food was fit to

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: eat or not.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: No, things like milk and juice as well.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: But actually, I thought it might be really good for drug storage in hospitals and

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: pharmacies.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: And coming back to food, maybe it'd be possible to use it for other things besides

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: freshness. Like how many kilograms a joint of meat is, for example.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: I was reading an article about food trends predicting how eating habits might change in

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: the next few years.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Oh things like more focus on local products?

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: That seems so obvious, but the shops are still full of imported foods.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Yes, they need to be more proactive to address that.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: One thing everyone's aware of is the need for a reduction in unnecessary packaging-but

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: just about everything you buy in supermarkets is still covered in plastic.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: The government needs to do something about it.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Do you think there'll be more interest in gluten and lactose-free food?

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: For people with allergies or food intolerances? I don't know.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Lots of people I know have been buying that type of food for years now.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Yes, even if they haven't been diagnosed with an allergy.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: That's right.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: One thing I 've noticed is the number of branded products related to celebrity chefs –

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: people watch them cooking on TV and then buy things like spice mixes or frozen foods with

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: the chef's name on. I bought something like that once, but I won't again.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Yeah – I bought a ready-made spice mix for chicken which was supposed to be used by a

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: chef I'd seen on television, and it didn't actually taste of anything.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Mm. Did the article mention 'ghost kitchens' used to produce takeaway food?

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Well, they might have the name of a restaurant, but actually they're a cooking facility

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: just for delivery meals – the public don't ever go there.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: But people aren't aware of that – it's all kept very quiet.

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: So people don't realise the food's not actually from the restaurant?

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Did you know more and more people are using all sorts of different mushrooms now, to

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: treat different health concerns? Things like heart problems?

cues.speaker: IN
cues.text: Yes, it's hard to know which varieties are safe to eat. Anyway maybe now...
